title: 5 Proven Ways to Reduce Late Rent Payments
excerpt: Late rent payments are the number one pain point for Nigerian landlords. Here are five practical strategies that actually work.
author: RentFlow Team
content:
Late rent payments cost Nigerian landlords billions of naira in lost income and stress every year. The good news? Most late payments are preventable with the right systems in place.

**1. Send automated reminders**
Automatic reminders 7 days, 3 days, and 1 day before rent is due significantly reduce forgetfulness. RentFlow sends these automatically via SMS and email.

**2. Make payment effortless**
The harder it is to pay, the more likely tenants will delay. With RentFlow, tenants pay in three taps — no bank queues, no WhatsApp back-and-forth.

**3. Be transparent about late fees**
Clearly communicate your late fee policy in the lease agreement. Tenants who know there is a consequence are more likely to pay on time.

**4. Offer multiple payment methods**
Card, bank transfer, Paystack — giving tenants options removes friction and excuses.

**5. Build a payment record**
When tenants have a visible payment history showing their track record, many take pride in keeping it clean.

title: Understanding Tenancy Agreements in Nigeria: A Landlord's Guide
excerpt: A solid tenancy agreement protects both you and your tenant. This guide covers what must be included under Nigerian law.
author: RentFlow Team
content:
A tenancy agreement is the backbone of any landlord-tenant relationship. Without one, disputes are almost impossible to resolve fairly.

**What must a tenancy agreement include?**
- Names of landlord and tenant(s)
- Property address and description
- Rent amount and due date
- Security deposit amount and conditions for return
- Lease duration (start and end date)
- Notice period for termination
- Maintenance responsibilities

**Tenancy Law in Nigeria**
The Tenancy Law of Lagos State 2011 is one of the most comprehensive in Nigeria. It limits advance rent demands to 1 year for residential properties. Similar protections exist in other states.

title: How to Handle Maintenance Requests Like a Professional Landlord
excerpt: How you respond to maintenance requests directly affects tenant retention. Here's a system that works.
author: RentFlow Team
content:
Maintenance requests handled badly are the leading reason tenants leave and leave bad word-of-mouth behind.

**The 24-hour acknowledgement rule**
Acknowledge every maintenance request within 24 hours — even if you can't fix it yet. Silence is the worst response.

**Categorise by priority**
Not all maintenance is equal. A broken security door is urgent; a squeaky hinge is not. RentFlow lets you assign priority levels so nothing urgent slips through.

**Keep tenants updated**
Once a contractor is booked, tell the tenant. Once the job is done, mark it resolved. Transparency builds trust.

**Use RentFlow's kanban board**
RentFlow's maintenance board gives you a clear view of every open request across all properties — received, in progress, resolved.
